URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/edinburgh-university-staff-strike-cuts-b3057125.html
The Independent — Ryan McDougall, published Monday 28 September 2026 00:01 BST (timestamp confirmed inside the article). Text via Exa search highlights.

Around 3,000 staff members at the University of Edinburgh are set to launch five weeks of industrial
action over £140 million in spending cuts and compulsory redundancies. Members of the University and
College Union begin their strike on Monday, with the disruption scheduled to last until 30 October.

The industrial action comes as the institution prepares to scrap 90 academic programmes, following an
announcement by university leadership two years ago outlining £140 million in savings alongside enforced
job losses. Unions estimate that 1,800 posts will ultimately be eliminated, though representatives noted
that senior management could halt the strike by agreeing to key demands.

UCU leaders are demanding an immediate guarantee against compulsory redundancies, a halt to cuts
targeting fixed-term and hourly-paid workers, a revised surplus target, and a focus on reducing capital
expenditure rather than staffing budgets.

UCU general secretary Jo Grady said: "Staff at Edinburgh have taken multiple days of strike action and
participated in a marking and assessment boycott but management have still, despite reserves over £3
billion, refused to rule out compulsory redundancies."

University principal Professor Sir Peter Mathieson said: "We are extremely disappointed that, despite
ongoing discussions, the University and College Union has announced five weeks' strike action, which
will unfairly and deliberately target our students' first semester of the academic year."
